Training data from reviewed questions

Source: R/questions.R
dragon_questions_dataset.Rd

Builds the dataset the fine-tune trains on: for every kept question, the k most relevant excerpts are retrieved from the documents (by the question, not the chunk it was written from, so training matches what happens at answer time) and placed in the prompt ahead of it; the answer is the response. This is the setup that beat a plain fine-tune in the prototypes: the model learns to use excerpts, and the documents stay the source of truth and can change later without retraining.

Usage

dragon_questions_dataset(qa, docs = NULL, k = 4, cite = TRUE, negatives = 0.15)

Arguments

qa

A dragon_questions data frame (only rows with keep = TRUE are used).

docs

The document set; defaults to the one the questions came from.

k

Excerpts per prompt.

cite

Append the excerpt number of the chunk each pair was written from to its answer (" [2]"), the way dragon_ask() cites, so the tuned model keeps citing. Answers that already contain a [n] marker are left alone. The source chunk is always among the excerpts: when retrieval misses it, it takes the last slot.

negatives

Share of extra rows, relative to the kept questions, in which a question is shown with excerpts from a different section of the documents and the response is "The documents do not cover this." Without them every training prompt has its answer in the excerpts, and fine-tuned models learn to answer everything. Tuned on R's manuals, a 0.5B, 1.5B, and 3B declined 0, 1, and 5 of 15 questions the manuals do not cover; with 15 percent negatives all three declined 15 of 15, and answered 26, 28, and 30 of 32 answerable questions, against 24, 29, and 30 without. 0 turns them off.

Value

A mapped dragon_dataset ready for dragon_train(). Its data has a negative column marking the "not covered" rows.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
docs <- dragon_documents(dragon_example_documents(), name = "policies")
qa <- dragon_questions(docs)
ds <- dragon_questions_dataset(qa)
dragon_preview(ds, n = 1)
}
